title: Unify embeddings + rerank pagination and HTTP error mapping for legacy clients
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: We continue to see integration issues from customers and legacy SDKs when migrating between older embeddings/rerank endpoints and the new unified API. Problems include mismatched pagination semantics (page/limit vs. cursor/next_cursor), inconsistent cursor encodings, and divergent HTTP error codes (400 vs 422 vs 500) for similar validation/semantic errors. This causes friction in migrations, flaky client code paths, and increased support tickets.

Proposal: Implement a compatibility layer in the API gateway and SDKs that provides: 1) a canonical cursor format (opaque, versioned) that both embeddings and rerank endpoints support; 2) deterministic mapping of legacy query params (page, per_page, offset) to cursor semantics; 3) standardized HTTP error mapping rules so identical validation failures produce the same status and structured error body across endpoints; 4) feature-flagged fallback behavior to preserve legacy error semantics per customer until migration is complete.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change core model ranking logic, nor does it attempt to unify response payload shapes beyond pagination and the top-level error contract. It also does not include full SDK releases for all languages (those are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical cursor format defined and documented (opaque base64 with version prefix).
Embeddings and rerank endpoints accept legacy params (page, limit, offset) and return next_cursor that translates deterministically to legacy semantics.

HTTP error mapping table implemented: validation -> 400, semantic mismatch -> 422, rate-limit -> 429, server errors -> 500; error body contains code, message, retriable boolean, and optional docs_url.
Backward-compatible feature flag allows per-customer legacy behavior for 6 months; default is new unified contract.
Automated integration tests covering cursor round-trip, legacy param translation, and error mappings for both endpoints exist in the API test harness.
SDK compatibility shim published for JS and Python with examples in the migration playbook.
Confluence migration guide and sample client snippets available and linked from the API docs.
No customer-facing incidents introduced during a canary rollout (canary cohort size <= 5% traffic).
implementation_notes: Gateway: implement translation middleware that detects legacy params and emits canonical next_cursor in response headers and body.
Runtime: ensure KV cache keys include cursor version to avoid cache poisoning between legacy and unified cursors.
SDKs: provide helper to convert legacy (page, limit) <-> cursor for JS and Python; mark helper as 'compat' in changelog.
Tests: add fuzz tests for cursor encoding/decoding and property-based tests for error mapping permutations.
Docs: update API reference, add migration playbook with step-by-step examples and rollbacks.
Observability: emit metric 'compat.pagination.translation.count' and histogram for translation latency; add SLO alert if translation latency > 50ms p95.
Telemetry: tag translated requests with header X-Compat-Mode:{legacy|unified} to measure adoption during rollout.
Rollout: implement feature flag gate in the control plane; beta customers can opt-in for early testing.
rollout_plan: 1) Spec published and API/SDK design review (2 weeks). 2) Gateway and runtime implementation behind feature flag; internal QA and integration tests (2 weeks). 3) Publish SDK compatibility shim + migration guide; invite 3 pilot customers to opt-in. 4) Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for 1 week, monitor errors and migration metrics. 5) Gradual ramp to 100% with automated rollback if key metrics regress. 6) Deprecation announcement for legacy behavior 6 months after full rollout.
